items.title: Adrian Cunningham interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 31, 2021
items.q: imitating Edmond Hall, trying to get close to how he would play the melody or how he would solo

ctx.x: I’m so glad you’re keeping it alive. You know? I’m trying to picture you and your trombone friend the first time, the first few times you tried to improvise. What was going through your head or what was your resources, or were you just like winging it?

I think it was a bit of all of the above. I think the first — because I was very much self- taught when I first discovered jazz. So I did probably what a lot of kids did, there was one record that I’m very grateful to hear because it’s still one of my favorites, it called “Ambassador Satch” and it’s the Louis Armstrong All-Stars 1955. It was a live concert they filmed, I think it was in Italy. And it was just an amaz — this was not a 78, this was a 33, this was a full record. And it was just, I loved the energy…
You weren’t annoyed by the clarinet like, you know, that quote “octave key” after learning the saxophone?
